subject: Seedling service incident: operator readout and action plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@seedling.health>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Repeated generation stalls this morning

Avery —

We saw repeated stalls in generation (50–90s tail latency spikes) across multiple customers between 08:50 and 09:05 PT this morning. Our ops team captured request IDs and a sample timeline (attached). Can you confirm whether this was on your side and, if so, what root cause you’re investigating? We’re starting an incident channel on our end and would like an operator-level readout for our SREs.

Thanks,
Elena
Ops Lead, Seedling Health
attachments: seedling_report_0930.csv
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@seedling.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated generation stalls this morning

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the sample request IDs. Ben (on infra) is pulling logs now. At a high level: we observed an elevated rate of soft failures and long-tail token latency in our inference tier starting ~08:48 PT, concentrated on a small subset of cached model shards. We’ve throttled traffic to affected hosts and are running a control to rebuild affected KV caches.

I’ll share an operator readout within the hour and a short timeline for your SREs. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your end-to-end SLA.

Next steps I’ll cover in the readout: timeline of events, concrete mitigations we executed, and immediate action items (including a temporary routing change and a KV cache eviction fix).

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@seedling.health>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Seedling incident: operator timeline (internal draft)

Team / Elena —

Attached is a draft CSV timeline we built from host and request logs (seedling_incident_timeline.csv). Key items:
- 08:46:12 PT: Background maintenance job triggered a delayed KV snapshot on a subset of nodes (non-deterministic overlap).
- 08:48:37 PT: First observed token latency spike for requests routed to those nodes.
- 08:50:10 PT: Retry storm on client side (backoff not applied uniformly) amplified load to healthy nodes leading to transient queueing.
- 08:53–09:02 PT: Our autoscaling and routing caught up; we applied an emergency KV cache eviction and pinned stable shard variants for Seedling traffic.
- 09:06 PT: Latency returned to baseline.

We also have a patch that prevents KV snapshot/eviction interactions in the short term (kvcache_patch.diff). Before I publish an official RCA, we want to run a quick validation on the patch in staging (planned 10/1 afternoon).

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: seedling_incident_timeline.csv, kvcache_patch.diff
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@seedling.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Seedling service incident — operator readout, RCA summary, and action items

Elena —

Per our conversation, please find below the operator-level readout and action plan. I’ve attached a concise RCA draft for review; once you confirm it’s shareable we’ll finalize and attach to your compliance portal.

RCA summary (short):
- What happened: A KV snapshot job overlapped with normal serving for a subset of shard hosts, which led to partial cache invalidation during peak request flow. That produced long-tail token latency for requests routed to those hosts. A subsequent client retry pattern increased pressure on other nodes, causing queueing and additional latency.
- Root cause: Uncoordinated KV snapshot/eviction interactions combined with an insufficiently conservative client backoff for long-tail responses.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:46 PT — scheduled snapshot job begins on 4 hosts in eu-west-1 (staggering bug caused same window).
- 08:48 PT — first token latency spikes observed from impacted hosts.
- 08:50 PT — amplification via client retries; queuing rises on healthy hosts.
- 08:53 PT — emergency KV cache eviction and temporary routing change executed.
- 09:06 PT — traffic and latency returned to baseline.

Immediate actions completed (short-term mitigations):
- Evicted affected KV caches and pinned stable shard variants for Seedling traffic (done 08:53–08:58 PT).
- Applied temporary routing rule to avoid the small host pool for 1 hour.
- Throttled non-critical background jobs during peak windows.

Planned actions (next 30 days):
1) Patch rollout: coordinate KV snapshot sequencing to prevent overlapping with serving windows; patch validated in staging — rollout to prod in a phased manner (Owner: Ben).
2) Backoff policy: partner with SDK team to push a client-side conservative backoff in the Seedling environment and publish recommended client settings (Owner: Neha).
3) Enhanced monitoring: add a long-tail token latency alert and a per-shard cache coherency monitor (Owner: Marissa).
4) Runbook update: update operator runbooks with KV snapshot/eviction checks and pre-rollout validation steps (Owner: Avery).

Attachments: seedling_rca_draft.pdf, seedling_incident_timeline.csv, kvcache_patch.diff

If you’re OK with the attached draft, we’ll finalize the RCA and upload to your compliance folder (link below). We can also schedule a 30-minute technical readout with our SREs + SDK engineer if your team wants deeper detail.

Link to draft and upload location: https://drive.redwood.ai/seedling/incident-2026-09-30
HubSpot ticket: HS-8739

Apologies again for the interruption — we’ll also follow up with a short post-deployment verification note after the patch goes live.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@seedling.health>

Cc: ops@seedling.health
Date: 2026-10-02T17:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seedling service incident — operator readout, RCA summary, and action items

Avery / team —

Thanks for the clear timeline and owners. A couple quick asks from Seedling SREs before you finalize the draft:
1) Can you add the concrete request IDs affected and correlate them to the timeline (we sent a subset in the first message; it’d be great to include complete mapping in the CSV).
2) Please confirm the planned prod rollout date for the KV snapshot sequencing patch and whether you’ll gate it on automated rollback on error.

Separately, given customer impact we’ll request a modest credit for the affected windows — can Marissa or whoever handles commercial remediation reach out so we can align?

If you’re available tomorrow morning we can do the 30-minute readout.

Thanks,
Elena
Ops Lead, Seedling Health
